title: Oven-roasted chicken tikka with rice and raita
description: Chicken pieces in a ginger, garlic and yogurt marinade with warm spices, roasted spread out on trays until browned. No tandoor needed. Inspired by Made in India by Meera Sodha.

steps.text: Pound or blend the ginger, garlic, chili and {1 tsp} of the salt into a paste. Cut the chicken into 3 cm chunks and coat it in the paste, {150 g} of the yogurt and all the spices. Leave for at least 15 minutes.
steps.tip: A few hours in the fridge makes it even more tender. The curry powder stands in for garam masala.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200 °C and oil two lined trays. Shake off the extra marinade and spread the chicken out with space between the pieces.
steps.tip: Crowded chicken steams in its yogurt and never browns.

steps.text: Roast for 20 minutes, turning halfway, until browned at the edges and cooked through.
steps.tip: Cut the biggest piece: no pink inside.

steps.text: Meanwhile start the rice: rinse it, put it in a pot with {500 ml} water and a pinch of salt, bring to the boil, then cover and cook on the lowest heat for 12 minutes. Leave it covered off the heat.
steps.tip: Keeping the lid on is what makes rice fluffy.

steps: Grate the cucumber, squeeze it and mix with the rest of the yogurt and salt. Serve the chicken with the rice and cucumber raita.

title: Eggplant and cherry tomato curry
description: Thin slices of eggplant simmered until they collapse into a thick, gently spiced tomato sauce with ginger, garlic and cumin. Inspired by Made in India by Meera Sodha.
steps: Soften the chopped onion in the oil for 7 minutes. Add the chopped chili, grated ginger and crushed garlic and fry for 3 minutes more.

steps.text: Add the halved tomatoes and salt and cook for 10 minutes until soft. Stir in the turmeric, cumin, coriander, tomato paste and sugar.
steps.tip: Cherry tomatoes give a sweet sharpness that big tomatoes do not.

steps.text: Add the eggplant, sliced into thin half moons, the drained chickpeas and {160 ml} warm water. Stir, cover and simmer gently for 20 minutes until the eggplant is completely soft.
steps.tip: Chickpeas are our addition, to make it a full meal. Stir now and then so it does not stick.

steps.text: Meanwhile start the rice: rinse it, put it in a pot with {500 ml} water and a pinch of salt, bring to the boil, then cover and cook on the lowest heat for 12 minutes. Leave it covered off the heat.
steps.tip: Keeping the lid on is what makes rice fluffy.

steps: Serve with the rice and yogurt.

title: Roast pumpkin curry with garlic and tomato
description: Pumpkin roasted until caramelised at the edges, then folded into a garlicky tomato curry with cumin and coriander. Inspired by Made in India by Meera Sodha.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200 °C. Peel the pumpkin, cut it into 2 cm slices, toss with {2 tbsp} of the oil, half the salt and the pepper and roast on two trays for 30 minutes, turning once.
steps.tip: Caramelised edges are the point, so give the slices room.

steps: Meanwhile fry the finely chopped onion in the rest of the oil for 10 minutes until browned. Pound the ginger, garlic and chili and fry for 2 minutes.

steps.text: Add the tomatoes, the rinsed lentils and {400 ml} water and simmer for 15 minutes until the lentils are soft. Stir in the sugar, coriander, cumin and the rest of the salt for 5 minutes.
steps.tip: The red lentils are our addition: they melt into the sauce and add protein.

steps.text: Meanwhile start the rice: rinse it, put it in a pot with {500 ml} water and a pinch of salt, bring to the boil, then cover and cook on the lowest heat for 12 minutes. Leave it covered off the heat.
steps.tip: Keeping the lid on is what makes rice fluffy.

steps: Fold the roasted pumpkin into the sauce gently, adding a splash of water if too thick. Serve with the rice and yogurt.

title: Gujarati potato curry with eggs
description: Potatoes cooked in a quick tomato sauce with cumin, coriander, turmeric and ginger, a simple everyday curry, served here with boiled eggs. Inspired by Made in India by Meera Sodha.
steps: Peel the potatoes and cut them into 2.5 cm cubes.

steps.text: Heat the oil and add {0.5 tsp} of the cumin. When it sizzles, add the grated ginger and chopped chili for 1 minute.
steps.tip: Mustard seeds crackling in the oil are the Gujarati touch, if you have some.

steps: Add the tomatoes, crushed, and cook for 10 minutes until thick.

steps.text: Stir in the turmeric, chili, coriander, the rest of the cumin, the sugar, salt, potatoes and {150 ml} warm water. Cover and cook for 15 minutes until a knife slides easily into the potatoes.
steps.tip: Stir gently now and then and add a splash of water if it catches.

steps: Meanwhile boil the eggs for 8 minutes, cool them in cold water and peel. Halve them and add to the curry.
Scatter with parsley and serve with warm flatbreads.

title: Home-style chicken curry with almonds
description: A family chicken curry: deep golden onions, ginger, garlic and tomato, softened with yogurt and thickened with ground almonds at the end. Inspired by Made in India by Meera Sodha.

steps.text: Warm the butter and oil with {1 tsp} of the cumin and the cinnamon, then add the finely chopped onions and cook for 12 minutes until deep golden.
steps.tip: A cinnamon stick is the original. Fish it out at the end if you use one.

steps: Pound the ginger, garlic and chili into a paste and fry it for 2 minutes.

steps.text: Add the passata, tomato paste, the rest of the cumin, the turmeric and salt and cook until thick and the oil separates.
steps.tip: The base should look glossy and paste-like before the yogurt goes in.

steps.text: Stir in the whisked yogurt a spoon at a time, then add the chicken. Cover and cook gently for 35 minutes, turning once.
steps.tip: Adding yogurt slowly stops it from splitting.

steps.text: Meanwhile start the rice: rinse it, put it in a pot with {500 ml} water and a pinch of salt, bring to the boil, then cover and cook on the lowest heat for 12 minutes. Leave it covered off the heat.
steps.tip: Keeping the lid on is what makes rice fluffy.

steps: Stir in the ground almonds and curry powder and cook for 5 minutes more until the chicken is cooked through. Serve with the rice.

title: Fish moilee (light coconut fish curry)
description: White fish fillets poached for a few minutes in a gentle coconut broth with ginger, garlic, onion, tomato and turmeric. Inspired by Made in India by Meera Sodha.
steps: Pound or blend the ginger, garlic, chili and a pinch of the salt into a paste.

steps.text: Start the rice: rinse it, put it in a pot with {500 ml} water and a pinch of salt, bring to the boil, then cover and cook on the lowest heat for 12 minutes. Leave it covered off the heat.
steps.tip: Keeping the lid on is what makes rice fluffy.

steps: Fry the thinly sliced onions in the oil in a wide pan for 8 minutes until soft and golden. Add the paste and fry for 2 minutes.
Add the quartered tomatoes, the rest of the salt, the turmeric and chili, cover and cook for 3 minutes.

steps.text: Pour in the coconut milk with {120 ml} water and bring to a gentle bubble. Lower in the fish, cover and cook for 5 to 7 minutes until it flakes.
steps.tip: A gentle bubble only: boiling hard breaks the fish.

steps: Squeeze over some lemon and serve with the rice and lemon wedges.

title: Salmon and spinach curry
description: Golden onions and whole spices with tomato, ginger and garlic, a big pile of spinach, and chunks of salmon simmered in at the end. Inspired by Made in India by Meera Sodha.
steps: Warm the cinnamon, cloves and a few peppercorns if you have them in the oil for 1 minute.

steps.text: Add the chopped onion and the sugar and cook for 12 minutes until golden.
steps.tip: The pinch of sugar helps the onion caramelise.

steps: Add the chopped tomatoes, cover and cook for 5 minutes. Stir in the grated ginger, crushed garlic and the rest of the spices and salt.

steps.text: Add the spinach in handfuls and cook for 8 minutes until wilted and well mixed with the sauce. Meanwhile start the rice: rinse it, put it in a pot with {500 ml} water and a pinch of salt, bring to the boil, then cover and cook on the lowest heat for 12 minutes.
steps.tip: It looks like a mountain of spinach, but it shrinks right down.

steps.text: Nestle the salmon, cut into chunks, into the sauce, cover and simmer for 5 to 7 minutes until just cooked. Serve with the rice.
steps.tip: Stir gently or not at all once the salmon is in, so the pieces stay whole.

title: Bombay eggs in spiced tomato and spinach
description: Eggs gently cooked in a thick sauce of fresh tomato, onion, toasted cumin and coriander, on a bed of spinach, with yogurt on top. Inspired by Made in India by Meera Sodha.

steps.text: Toast the cumin and coriander in a dry wide pan for 1 minute until fragrant.
steps.tip: Whole seeds crushed after toasting are even better, if you have them.

steps: Add the oil and the sliced onions and fry for 7 minutes, then the crushed garlic and grated ginger for 2 minutes.

steps.text: Add the diced tomatoes and simmer for 15 minutes until thick. Stir in the tomato paste, salt, sugar, chili and turmeric.
steps.tip: The sauce should be thick enough for a spoon to leave a trail.

steps: Stir in the spinach until wilted, then make 6 hollows in the sauce.

steps.text: Crack an egg into each, cover and cook on low for 8 to 10 minutes until the whites are set.
steps.tip: Take it off the heat while the yolks still wobble if you like them runny.

steps: Top with pepper, parsley and spoons of yogurt and serve from the pan with warm flatbreads.

title: Quick kidney bean curry
description: Kidney beans in a warm onion, ginger and tomato sauce scented with cinnamon and cumin. A fast, filling weeknight curry from the cupboard. Inspired by Made in India by Meera Sodha.

steps.text: Start the rice: rinse it, put it in a pot with {500 ml} water and a pinch of salt, bring to the boil, then cover and cook on the lowest heat for 12 minutes. Leave it covered off the heat.
steps.tip: Keeping the lid on is what makes rice fluffy.

steps: Warm the cinnamon and cumin in the oil for 1 minute.
Add the chopped onion and fry for 8 minutes until golden, then the grated ginger, crushed garlic and chopped chili for 2 minutes.

steps.text: Stir in the tomato paste, sugar, salt, curry powder and turmeric for 2 minutes.
steps.tip: Frying the paste and spices briefly gives the sauce its depth.

steps.text: Add the drained beans and {200 ml} warm water and simmer for 5 to 8 minutes until saucy. Serve with the rice and yogurt.
steps.tip: It keeps 3 days and freezes well.

title: Indian fried rice with peas and egg
description: Leftover rice fried with golden onion, garlic, cumin, turmeric, peas and any cooked vegetables, finished with egg, spring onion and lemon. Inspired by Made in India by Meera Sodha.

steps.text: If you have no leftover rice, cook it ahead: rinse it, cook it in {550 ml} water with the lid on for 12 minutes, spread it out to cool and chill it.
steps.tip: Cold rice fries into separate grains. Warm rice turns sticky.

steps: Fry the chopped onion in the oil in a wok or large pan for 10 minutes until golden. Add the chopped garlic and cumin for 1 minute.
Stir in the turmeric and chili, then the vegetables, and cook for 5 minutes until hot.

steps.text: Push everything to one side, pour the beaten eggs into the space and scramble them, then mix them in.
steps.tip: Eggs are our addition, for protein.

steps.text: Add the peas, rice and salt and fry for 6 to 8 minutes, stirring, until piping hot throughout.
steps.tip: Go easy on the salt if your rice was already salted.

steps: Scatter with spring onion, squeeze over the lemon and serve with yogurt.
